about: How well human professional fortune tellers actually scored on these exact questions. Transcribed from the organizer's published results. This is a real human baseline: entrants were practising masters competing publicly under their own names for a trophy, on questions whose answers were sealed until after the contest closed.
caveats: Only the top finishers' scores are published. The mean over all entrants is not known for any edition, so these numbers are a ceiling, not an average.

Entrant counts are not published for most editions, so the ceiling is not comparable across editions: a top score drawn from 200 entrants is a higher-order statistic than the same score drawn from 20.

From the 9th edition on, the official ranking is not the raw score. The rule is diving-style: each entrant's best-scoring case and worst-scoring case are dropped, leaving the middle six cases (30 of 40 questions). Both figures are given below where published; `raw` is the one comparable to running a model over all items in this dataset.
Editions differ in option count, so the random-guess baseline differs (see `random_baseline`).
